title: Forklift Inspection Checklist (29 CFR 1910.178)
subtitle: For the examination before a truck is placed in service and for site audits of forklift operations.
instructions: Mark every item OK, Defect or N/A.
If an item affecting safety fails, take the truck out of service, report the defect and keep the truck out of use until it is repaired (1910.178(p)(1) and (q)(7)).
The manufacturer's instructions and your site rules may add checks to this list.

sections.title: Truck condition and markings
items: All nameplates and markings are in place and legible
Approved truck carries the testing laboratory's label or identifying mark
Any modification affecting capacity or safe operation has the manufacturer's prior written approval, and the capacity, operation and maintenance plates match it
Truck is marked with the attachment and the approximate combined weight at maximum elevation with the load laterally centered
High lift rider truck has an overhead guard fitted, unless operating conditions do not permit one
Vertical load backrest extension fitted where the type of load presents a hazard
No leaks anywhere in the fuel system
Water supply is not below 75 percent of filled capacity
No hazardous sparks or flames from the exhaust system
Truck is free of lint, excess oil and grease

sections.title: Examination, defects and repairs
items: Truck examined before being placed in service and at least daily
Trucks used round the clock are examined after each shift
Defects found are reported immediately and corrected
Any truck needing repair, defective or unsafe is out of service until restored to safe operating condition
Repairs are made only by authorized personnel
Replacement parts are equivalent as to safety with the original design
No part runs above its normal operating temperature; an overheating truck stays out of service until the cause is eliminated

sections.title: Operator training and certification
items: Every operator completed training before driving, other than for training purposes
Record names the operator, gives the training date and evaluation date, and identifies who trained or evaluated
Each operator's performance evaluated within the last three years
Refresher training given after unsafe operation, an accident or near-miss, a failed evaluation, assignment to a different truck type, or a workplace change affecting safe operation
Trainees drive only under direct supervision of a qualified trainer and where no one is endangered

sections.title: Battery charging and refueling
items: Charging installation is in an area designated for that purpose
Electrolyte flushing and neutralizing, fire protection, charger protection from trucks, and ventilation for battery fumes are provided
Conveyor, overhead hoist or equivalent equipment provided for handling batteries
Truck properly positioned and brake applied before batteries are changed or charged
Battery vent caps are functioning and battery (or compartment) covers are open to dissipate heat
Smoking is prohibited in the charging area
Precautions in place to prevent open flames, sparks or electric arcs in the charging area
Tools and other metallic objects kept away from the top of uncovered batteries
Engine is off whenever the fuel tank is filled

sections.title: Operating area and work practices
items: Atmosphere or location has been classified as hazardous or nonhazardous before trucks are used there
Only approved trucks are used in hazardous locations
Auxiliary directional lighting on the truck where general lighting is less than 2 lumens per square foot
Carbon monoxide from truck operations does not exceed the levels in 1910.1000
Fire aisles, stairway access and fire equipment are clear
Sufficient headroom under lights, pipes, sprinklers and other overhead installations
Brakes set and wheel chocks under the rear wheels while the trailer is boarded
Wheel stops or other recognized positive protection keep railroad cars from moving during loading
Dockboards and bridge plates are secured before being driven over
Forks fully lowered, controls neutral, power off and brakes set; wheels blocked on an incline

references: 29 CFR 1910.178: Powered industrial trucks (Part 1910 Subpart N, Materials Handling and Storage)
disclaimer: General guidance only, not legal advice. Check the current regulation and your employer's procedures.
